speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The resolutions in that Motion relating to Mr Singh were all dealt with and concluded on that day.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members will recall that in the fifth limb of that Motion, this House noted "that the High Court judgment and the Committee's findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, which have to be considered separately".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is unfinished business which has to be dealt with.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To recap briefly, a key issue in the COP inquiry was what was said at the meeting of 8 August 2021 between Ms Khan and the three senior Workers' Party (WP) leaders: Mr Pritam Singh, Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In particular, whether Ms Khan was told to suppress the fact that she had told an untruth in Parliament, that is, that she should "take it to the grave".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As the findings against Mr Singh were the most serious, the House referred his case to the Public Prosecutor.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This enabled the matter to be independently investigated and if charges were brought, Mr Singh would be able to defend himself with the benefit of legal representation, and it would be for the Court to determine whether the charges were proven beyond reasonable doubt.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In relation to Ms Lim and Mr Faisal, the Committee found that they had lied about what was said at the meeting of 8 August.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Report stated, and I quote, "Ms Lim and Mr Faisal attended the 8 August meeting.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They agreed (to Mr Singh's advice) that the Untruth should be buried, and that Ms Khan would not have to tell the truth.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: They did not tell the truth to the Committee about that meeting." However, the Committee considered Ms Lim's and Mr Faisal's roles in the matter to be subsidiary, and noted that both had been somewhat helpful to the Committee, albeit in a limited way.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Committee therefore recommended that consideration of what, if anything, should be done about their conduct of stating untruths to the Committee should be deferred until the conclusion of investigations and/or criminal proceedings against Mr Singh.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was done to be fair to Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: If the investigations or court proceedings produced evidence inconsistent with the Committee's findings, Parliament could take that into account before deciding what, if any, action should be taken.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Pending that process, Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were given the benefit of the doubt.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The criminal proceedings against Mr Singh concluded on 4 December 2025 when the High Court Judgement was delivered.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On 14 January 2026, Parliament passed a resolution noting that the High Court Judgement and the Committee's findings had implications for Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: During the Committee hearings: (a) Ms Lim denied that Mr Singh had told Ms Khan to take her Untruth to the grave.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: She said that there was no discussion on this point.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (b) Mr Faisal's evidence was that all three WP leaders did not remark on Ms Khan's confession that she had lied and did not discuss what to do about it.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (c) Thus, at the COP hearings, both Ms Lim and Mr Faisal denied that Mr Singh had advised Ms Khan to take her lie to the grave, and said that the matter was not discussed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, now, after a full investigation, trial and appeal dealing with this issue, the Courts have expressly and conclusively found that:  (a) At the 8 August 2021 meeting – at which all three WP leaders were present – Ms Khan's Untruth was discussed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: (b) Mr Singh had lied when he denied that he told Ms Khan to "take it to the grave" – "it" meaning her Untruth.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Courts' findings directly contradict Ms Lim's and Mr Faisal's evidence.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It follows logically from the Courts' findings that their evidence to the Committee was not true.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Court Judgment effectively confirmed the findings of the Committee in relation to Ms Lim and Mr Faisal.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The question that arises is what is to be done in light of this.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is the unresolved issue that was deferred for decision.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In principle, if someone gave untrue evidence to a Committee of Parliament and did so knowingly or intentionally, this would be dishonourable conduct and a serious contempt of Parliament and would be dealt with under the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962 (or PPIPA).

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Ordinarily, if there is evidence someone has lied to a Select Committee, I would initiate the PPIPA process for dealing with such conduct.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, there are certain timelines within which such action must take place.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In most cases, offences under the PPIPA can be dealt with fairly quickly and in the same session of Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Occasionally, the offence may occur in one session of Parliament but for whatever reason Parliament may not be able to deal with it immediately and it is dealt with in a subsequent session of Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, in the interests of finality, there are constraints on this.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The previous Parliament – that is the 14th Parliament – was first constituted on 24 August 2020.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It was prorogued on 24 March 2023 and re-opened on 10 April 2023.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this case, the relevant conduct of Ms Lim and Mr Faisal took place in 2021, during the First Session of the 14th Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Singh was convicted by the District Court on 17 February 2025.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was during the Second Session of the 14th Parliament.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, Parliament rightly deferred consideration of Ms Lim's and Mr Faisal’s cases until the Court process had concluded.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those proceedings concluded only on 4 December 2025, when the High Court delivered its judgment.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By then, the 14th Parliament had been dissolved, a General Election had taken place, and the 15th Parliament had begun.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This does not mean that Parliament is without recourse.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The House could, if it wished, pass a Motion to express regret at such conduct.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such a Motion would serve to signal Parliament's disapproval, as it did in Mr Singh's case in January this year.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, it should be noted that in the January Motion, this House had already signalled its clear disapproval of lying to Parliament or its Committees.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Had the timelines been different, I would have proposed a different course of action.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This outcome has happened because even though this House was entitled to act on the Committee's findings in 2021, it decided to give Ms Lim and Mr Faisal the benefit of the doubt for the time being.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even though the Committee's findings have now been effectively confirmed by the High Court Judgment, the law in this case, the time-bar provisions of the PPIPA must be observed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Unless any Member objects, we can now bring this matter to a close.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Before I call on hon Members for clarifications if any, I should point out that pursuant to Standing Order 23, Members may seek clarification on the Ministerial Statement, but no debate shall be allowed thereon.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Members can seek clarifications by way of asking questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I seek Members' understanding to keep your clarifications clear and concise, so that the Leader of the House can answer as many clarifications as possible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And likewise, when she made those statements on 14 January, I had also responded on 14 January, and my statements are on record.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs.
